newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan cement, transport shares up at mid-session.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan cement, transport shares up at mid-session.

text.p: Taiwan's cement and transport shares rose at mid-morning on Thursday on hopes for a property market recovery and an imminent end to Taiwan's ban on direct shipping links with rival China, brokers said.
With 70 minutes left, shares in the cement sector were up 1.88 percent, while transport shares were up 0.95 percent.
Associated Transport rose to its uplimit of seven percent to T$36.7, gaining T$2.4., while Yang Ming Marine gained T$1.4 to T$39.4.
Chia Hsin Cement gained T$1.5 to T$31. Chien Tai cement earned T$0.8 at T$22.7, brokers said.
"Investors hold an optimistic view toward the transport shares on the improving future of shipping links with mainland China," Chen Han-chung, manager of Yungli Securities said.
Taiwan media reported on Thursday that China would soon allow several Taiwan shippers to begin operating Taiwan-mainland shipping routes.
Investors' anticipation of a property market recovery after years of recession was the main factor behind the cement sector rise, brokers said.
